{"number":1225,"title":"The hourly scheduler cron is the fleet's whole Actions allowance — move to a twice-daily tick","body":"## The problem

The August usage report puts `claudinite-scheduler.yml` at 1,515 of 2,123 private Actions minutes — **71% of spend** — running at a near-identical ~26 min/day on every private member (MissingBulbWebsite 26.1, WIP 27.0, hitbut 26.0, ClaudiniteWebsite 25.2, EdFringeAllocator 17.0).

Four private members × 24 min/day × 30d = 2,880 min = **$17.28/mo**, which is exactly the $18.00 allowance the report terminates at. The scheduler *is* the allowance, with zero macOS and zero real work. It scales linearly with adoption: WIP and hitbut came online Aug 20–21 and immediately added ~53 min/day between them.

## Why optimising the job buys nothing

Sampled 30 consecutive scheduled runs on this repo: **median 32s wall-clock**, only one over 60s. Actions bills each job rounded up to the whole minute, so ~46% of every billed minute is already rounding waste.

The cost is **run count**, not compute. The only lever is fewer runs.

## What the 24 runs/day are actually buying

Exactly one task in the corpus is `hourly` — `usage-fold` (`packs/claudinite-growth`). Everything else is `daily-2h`/`daily-1h`/`daily`/`daily+1h`/`weekly`/`monthly`/`manual`. Per `engine/scheduler/calendar.mjs`, the whole daily family lands at `dailyHour-2 … dailyHour+1`, with weekly and monthly also at `dailyHour` — so a default member's entire anchor set is four clock hours a day.

Two of the three remaining jobs are already solved elsewhere in the engine:

- **Ordering within a repo.** `after:` shipped (`engine/scheduler/task-contract.mjs:184-192`); `growth-extract` declares it and its own comment says the staggered hours *"express the same intent and cannot enforce it; this can."*
- **Chain continuation.** `executor.mjs:215` re-reads the queue each iteration and calls `readyDependents()` on every close, so a multi-stage chain drains back-to-back in one run.

That leaves adopting newly-marked ad-hoc issues, `Not-before` releases, and dead-claim reclaims as the only work the 23 extra runs a day exist for.

## The end state

`docs/tasks-dispatch/DESIGN.md` §17, with the measured trade and the rejected alternatives. Cron fires twice daily at ` ,<(dailyHour+12)%24>`. **24 runs/day → 2**; $17.28/mo → $1.44/mo; a new private member costs 2 min/day instead of 26.

---

# The plan

## Phase 0 — out-of-band setup: **none**

Verified there is no human-only step. No new secret, permission, repo variable or platform setting. The one path a converge cannot push into is `.github/workflows/`, and that is already solved: `pendingSchedulerWorkflow` (`updates/pack-update.mjs:161`) computes the target and **withholds** it, and the `update` task's apply stage lands it through the member's own PR lane. The cron rewrite reaches every member on the existing nightly cycle with nobody in the loop.

## Phase 1 — the approved stack (one review pass)

All code written before approval is asked for, including the destructive tail.

- [ ] **PR A — #1226 (open).** Design + simulator: `cronHours`, S67–S73, DESIGN §17, coverage rows. Closes #1227.
      *Exit:* merged.
- [ ] **PR B — the vocabulary.** Split `FREQUENCIES` (what a NEW declaration may name) from an accept-at-the-door set, with **one normalization door at declaration load** — not inside `anchorInstant`, because `periodMs` also feeds the janitor's stale-ready bound (`queue/janitor-rules.mjs:103`) and the signal window (`queue/signals.mjs:15`); normalizing only the anchor judges a daily task stale after two hours. Four consumers: `calendar.mjs:25`, `task-contract.mjs:100`, `packs/claudinite-growth/task-declaration-shape.mjs:49` (rejects the retired tokens for new declarations), `slots.mjs:23` (fielded shim, stays).
      Four declarations move: `update` `daily-2h`→`daily`; `growth-extract` `daily-1h`→`daily` (already has `after:`); `fleet-digest` `daily+1h`→`daily` + a new `after:` naming the sheepdog sweeps (safe cross-pack — an undeclared upstream yields no constraint); `usage-fold` `hourly`→`daily` **and its `WINDOW_DAYS = 2/24` must move with it**, or the "session captured" half of its precondition goes permanently dark and a repo whose only movement is commit-less sessions never folds again.
      Plus the cross-repo stagger `after:` cannot express: **set this repo's `taskScheduler.dailyHour` to 5**, so members extract at 04:00 and the canon's `growth-promote` reads their merged mains at 05:00. One line, this repo only, no fleet migration. Add `after: ['claudinite-growth/growth-extract']` to the canon-local `growth-promote` for the within-repo half.
      *Exit:* merged, suite green, S74 (normalized `hourly` behaves as `daily`) added and passing.
- [ ] **PR C — the cron.** `hashedCron` returns two hours derived from `dailyHour`; `converge-wiring.mjs:132` passes the schedule; the vendored stub's placeholder and **the canon's own `.github/workflows/claudinite-scheduler.yml` change in the same commit** — the canon has no converge, so its copy drifts invisibly otherwise.
      *Exit:* merged; this repo's own workflow reads the two-hour cron.
- [ ] **PR D — the destructive tail, written now, merged later.** Retire the door-normalization and drop the legacy tokens from the accepted set. Body states its merge is gated on Link 3 and names it.
      *Exit:* approved in this pass; **not merged**.

## Phase 2 — the execution chain

Filed as sub-issues of this tracker once the plan is agreed, each naming the previous in `Blocked-by:` so the queue does the waiting.

- [ ] **Link 1 — force delivery and read it back.** Drive Shepherd's `fleet-baseline` with `follow`.
      *Ready when:* PRs B and C are merged.
      *Worked when:* every member's stamp shows the new `packVersions`, **and** its `.github/workflows/claudinite-scheduler.yml` cron reads ` H,H+12` for that member's own `dailyHour`. Read per member; a member that cannot be read parks the link open rather than passing — a scope-blocked sweep answers "all clear" exactly like a healthy one.
- [ ] **Link 2 — verify in production.** *Ready when:* Link 1 closed and one full UTC day has passed.
      *Worked when:* each private member's Actions usage shows exactly **2** scheduler runs for that day (baseline: 24), and no task's standing item is missing its occurrence. Also the first read of the risk the sim cannot model — whether a member's whole daily chain now fits one drain against `timeout-minutes: 350`.
- [ ] **Link 3 — retire the tolerance.** *Ready when:* Link 2 closed **and** no member's task declarations still name a retired token — a converge-confirmable precondition, never a calendar date: retiring it while a member still declares `hourly` turns that member's daily task into a two-hour staleness park.
      *Worked when:* PR D merged, suite green.

## Known residual risks

- **Dropped ticks cost 12× more latency** (S71). Nothing is stranded — dueness comes from the anchor, never from whether the cron fired — but a dropped anchor tick now waits until the drain tick. This is why the second tick is not optional.
- **Ad-hoc latency goes to a 6h mean / 12h worst case** (S68). An `issues: [labeled]` trigger would take it to seconds for a run only when a mark happens; recorded in §17.5 as additive and deliberately out of this plan's scope.
- **A whole day now settles serially in one Actions job.** The simulator's durations are fixtures, so it cannot say whether a real member's chain fits. Link 2 is the first real measurement.

{"number":1235,"title":"Chain 1/3: force the twice-daily cron onto every member, and read it back","body":"Link 1 of #1225's execution chain. You will never see the conversation that planned this — everything you need is here.

```
Blocked-by: #1231
Model: sonnet
```

## What changed, and why this needs forcing

The scheduler cron went from hourly to twice daily (`docs/tasks-dispatch/DESIGN.md` §17): ` ,<(dailyHour+12)%24> * * *`. That is a change to a contract members' own files must satisfy — a workflow file plus a frequency vocabulary — so the nightly converge is not enough on its own to answer *"did it work on every repo?"*.

## What makes this step's world ready

#1231 closed, meaning #1230 merged. The queue holds this until then.

## The playbook

1. Drive Shepherd's `fleet-baseline` with `follow`, so it converges every member and reports per member rather than dispatching and returning.
2. For **each** member, read two things from the member's own repo:
   - its stamp's `packVersions` — `claudinite-lifecycle` ≥ `60822.2`, `claudinite-growth` ≥ `60822.1`, `claudinite-dashboard` ≥ `60822.2`;
   - its `.github/workflows/claudinite-scheduler.yml` `cron:` line.
3. The cron is member-specific. Compute the expected value rather than matching a constant: `node engine/scheduler/hash-minute.mjs ` for the minute, and the member's own `taskScheduler.dailyHour` (default 4) for the hours — so a default member expects ` 4,16 * * *`.

## What counts as this step having worked

Every member reads back **both** the stamped pack versions and its own correct two-tick cron.

The workflow file is the half that can lag: `.github/workflows/` is the one path a converge cannot push, so it lands through the member's `update` task apply-stage PR. A member whose stamp has moved but whose workflow PR is still open has **not** passed — note it and keep this issue open; it will pass on a later run once that PR lands.

## When the check fails

Comment what you actually read, per member, and **leave this issue open**. Closing is what releases the next link, so a failed step must not close.

A member you cannot read is a failure, not a pass. A scope-blocked or rate-limited sweep answers "all clear" in exactly the way a healthy fleet does — if a read did not succeed, say so rather than counting it.

## How it ends

Comment the per-member evidence on #1225, then close this issue as completed. That close releases Link 2.

{"number":1233,"title":"Retire the twice-daily-cron migration tolerances","body":"Phase D of #1225 — the destructive tail. Written and reviewed with the rest of the stack; **merged only when the chain's preconditions read true**, never on a date.

Two tolerances, two gates:

- **The frequency tolerance.** `LEGACY_FREQUENCIES` empties, so `ACCEPTED_FREQUENCIES` collapses onto `FREQUENCIES` and a declaration still naming `hourly`/`daily±Nh` fails contract validation. *Gate:* no member's own task declarations still name a retired token. {"number":1220,"title":"Verify in production: the executor's between-items hold read, and the invocation drop","body":"#1218 made an executor run drain the queue instead of settling one item, and had it re-read the operator hold between items via `GET /repos/{repo}/actions/variables/CLAUDINITE_TASKS_SUSPEND_ALL`. Every part of that is covered by tests that ran — except one thing no test can settle: **whether the Actions `GITHUB_TOKEN` is allowed to make that read at all.** The workflow `permissions:` block has no key for variables access, and the session that wrote it could not reach `api.github.com` to check the docs, so the code was written to degrade rather than guess: on any non-200 it falls back to the value the run started with and logs the access it lacked. That fallback is correct either way, but which branch actually runs is unknown until a real drain makes the call.

The second read below is the change's own premise — that the invocation count drops — which is only true in production by construction.

```
Original-issue: #1214
In-production-when: a `Claudinite executor` workflow run in missingbulb/Claudinite that started after 2026-08-22T10:25Z (the merge of #1218) has finished, AND its log shows it settled at least one item (a line matching `^- #\d+:` in the run's final summary). The between-items read only happens after a settle, so a run that found nothing pickable proves nothing and does not satisfy this.
Verify: read that run's log. (1) If it contains `could not read CLAUDINITE_TASKS_SUSPEND_ALL live`, the token CANNOT read repository variables: the between-items hold is inert and the operator hold gates run starts only, as it did before #1218 — record the exact status code from the log line, comment it here, and reopen Original-issue so the fallback can be made the documented behaviour (DESIGN §8 already states this outcome as possible; it would become the actual one). If the line is absent, the live read works — comment saying so, quoting the run URL. Either result is a pass: this verification exists to learn which. You are triaging GitHub issues in repo missingbulb/Claudinite as part of the `tidy-issues` maintenance task. Use ONLY the mcp__github__* MCP tools for GitHub access (issue_read, issue_write, add_issue_comment, get_label, list_issue_fields). You also have local repo access at /home/user/Claudinite (already `git fetch origin main`-ed; origin/main tip is e26e0c188fbd7b11c702babc89d4014bda1f4716) via Bash/Grep/Read — use `git show origin/main:<path>` or `git grep <pattern> origin/main -- <path>` to check what's actually true of main's CURRENT content. Do not check out or modify any branch; read-only against origin/main.
```

Triage EACH of these issue numbers, one at a time, independently: 1119, 1169, 1188, 1184, 1166, 1161, 1160, 1154, 1050, 1096

## The triage ladder — take the FIRST applicable action per issue

1. **Already implemented in `main`** → verify the issue's actual ask is true of origin/main's content NOW (never infer from a linked PR merging or the issue "looking" done) → **close** it (issue_write: state=closed, state_reason=completed) + post a one-line comment citing exactly where/how it's true in main (file/behavior), ending with the marker below.
2. **Conflicts with a current guideline/rule in the repo** (e.g. contradicts something in CLAUDE.md / packs/*/RULES.md as currently written) → apply label `needs-decision` (get current labels first — see label-safety note below) + comment naming the conflict, ending with the marker.
3. **Blocked by another issue** (that other issue is open and must land first) → apply label `blocked` + comment `blocked by #N`, ending with the marker.
4. **Small and quick to do** (a well-scoped, low-risk change) → apply label `quick-win` + comment scoping what the quick fix is, ending with the marker.
5. **Else** → leave it untouched. Take no action, post nothing.

### Checkbox signal
If EVERY checkbox in the issue body is ticked, that's the author's own claim of completion — a reason to run the "implemented in main" check (rung 1), never proof by itself. Verified true in main ⇒ close citing where. Not verified ⇒ comment naming what's still missing (this IS an action — it's a comment, so log it, but do NOT close). A partially-ticked list is not a completion signal at all — triage as if no boxes existed. If the ask has NO repo-side artifact (e.g., a console/platform setting only a human can touch), the author's own ticks are the closing condition — say so in your comment and close.

### Never re-post a verdict already posted
Before doing anything, read the issue's existing comments (issue_read method=get_comments). Find the most recent comment ending in a `<!-- claudinite:tidy-issues verdict=... -->` marker (or, for an issue triaged before the marker existed, one that clearly restates this same verdict in wording). If the action you're about to take is the SAME action that comment already announced, take NO action and NO comment — record this issue's outcome as `unchanged` (note: "<action> since <date>"). Closing is never a repeat — it changes the issue's actual state, so if the issue is still open and your verdict is "close", always execute the close even if a prior comment argued for it.

### Marker
End every comment you post (whether it's a close comment, needs-decision, blocked, quick-win, or a "still missing" comment) with this exact line alone at the end:
```
<!-- claudinite:tidy-issues verdict=<action> -->
```
where `<action>` is one of: closed, needs-decision, blocked, quick-win (use `closed` even for the "still missing, not closing" case is WRONG — for that case, since you did NOT close, there is no verdict action from the ladder; skip posting a marker-bearing comment for that sub-case only if you're unsure, but generally: if you post a comment about missing work under the checkbox path without closing, treat it as a regular open triage note and do not apply a verdict marker since it isn't a ladder outcome — just leave it uncommented in that edge case and record it as `left`).

### Label safety
GitHub's issue-update label field REPLACES the full label set, it doesn't add to it. Before applying `needs-decision`/`blocked`/`quick-win`, call issue_read method=get_labels to get the issue's CURRENT labels, then call issue_write method=update with labels = (existing labels ∪ {new label}), deduplicated. If get_label shows the label doesn't exist in the repo yet, still include it in the issue_write labels array (GitHub auto-creates on issue update in most configs); if the write errors, note the failure in your report but still post the comment (the comment is the actual triage signal).

## What NOT to do
- Never touch PRs, branches, or push code. Never comment on or close a PR even if a number here happens to be one (check first: issue_read get gets you `pull_request`-shaped data if it's actually a PR — if so, skip it and note "is a PR, not an issue, skipped").
- Never invent implementation status — cite exact file paths / content from origin/main.
- Don't over-post: if uncertain, prefer "left" over guessing.

## Output format
When done with all 10 issues, report back a plain list, one line per issue, EXACTLY in this format:
`#<number>: <action> — <one-sentence note>`
where `<action>` is one of: closed, needs-decision, blocked, quick-win, left, unchanged, skipped-pr.
This is your entire deliverable — return just this list (10 lines), nothing else.

- session-start-hook: Creating and developing startup hooks for Claude Code on the web. Use when the user wants to set up a repository for Claude Code on the web, create a SessionStart hook to ensure their project can run tests and linters during web sessions.

- adopt-pack: Add one or more packs to an already-adopted Claudinite member — declare, run each pack's adoption interview, re-vendor, scaffold, land. Use when asked to adopt, add, enable, or declare a pack (e.g. product-wiki, executable-requirements) on a repo that already runs Claudinite.
- authoring-agent-docs: How to write instruction files coding agents follow reliably. Use before writing or editing any Claude instruction doc — a project CLAUDE.md, a convention doc, a routine spec.
- bug-investigation: Method for investigating a bug and pinning down its root cause. Use when investigating a bug report, when a fix didn't hold or a bug recurs, or when a report doesn't reproduce against main.

- extract-from-activity: Mine a window of a repo's commits, merged PRs and issue activity for durable, reusable lessons and land them in the repo's own local packs. - extract-from-conversations: Mine an agent-user conversation — a captured conversation log or the live session — for friction-driven lessons (misunderstandings, backtracks, measured wall-time waits) and land them in the repo's own local packs. - file-placement: Where a file should live — the reference-distance metric, the high-reach code smell, and the mandated-location, test-location and plugin-contract exemptions. Use before placing, moving, or renaming a file, or when reviewing where one lives.

- prose-to-checks: Mine pack prose (RULES.md, SKILL.md) for always-testable rules that were never converted to checks, and convert the strongest ones. - repo-text-sweeps: Mechanics for grep/sed sweeps, renames, and path relocations across a repo. Use before a bulk find-replace, a rename, or moving files — and after one, to catch silently broken references.

- single-pr-status: Assess one open pull request's landed status — keep-open, or closeable (merged, already-in-main, superseded, stale) — read-only. {"number":276,"title":"Move chrome-extension-release plumbing out of core `.github/` into the pack (vendored into consumers)","body":"Resolves the **RELEASE** item of #270: the reusable release workflows (`.github/workflows/chrome-extension-*.yml` + `deploy-privacy-page.yml`) and the three composite actions (`read-release-config`, `bump-extension-patch`, `report-failure`) live in Claudinite's core tree but exist solely for the `chrome-extension-release` pack. They must move behind the pack that owns them, leaving Claudinite with no release-specific GitHub Actions.

## Decision (agreed with owner)

- **Hosting model: vendor into each consumer.** GitHub only resolves reusable workflows/composite actions from a repo's own `.github/`, never from a `packs/…` subdir, so "into the pack" means the pack holds the templates and each consumer hosts a *managed* copy in its own `.github/`. Consumers become self-contained; baselining (not the consumer) owns keeping the copies correct. This reverses the original "thin consumer" design — deliberately.
- **Phase-2 deletion: automatic, telemetry-gated.** Once the fleet census confirms every consumer has vendored, the census deletes Claudinite's release plumbing automatically as part of migration retirement — no follow-up PR.
- **Secrets: nothing to migrate.** The four `CHROME_*` secrets already live in each consumer repo (they travel via `secrets: inherit` from the consumer's own workflow); Claudinite holds none.

## Plan

1. **Pack = source of truth.** Move the 4 workflows + 3 composite actions into `packs/chrome-extension-release/` as vendored templates; rewrite cross-repo `uses: missingbulb/Claudinite/.github/…@main` → local `uses: ./.github/…`; rename to avoid the in-repo filename collision (the orchestrator and the create-package reusable are both `chrome-extension-release.yml` today).
2. **Migration is the fix vehicle.** A new baseline migration carries: (a) a **materialize** op — baselining writes the vendored set into each consumer's `.github/` and drops the old thin-stub `@main` refs; (b) a **legacyPresent** probe ("still references `missingbulb/Claudinite/.github/workflows/chrome-extension-*`") for fleet telemetry; (c) a **retire-deletes-from-home** list — Claudinite's own release files. Extend the migration mechanism (today rename-only) with the materialize op, and teach the census to delete the home-repo files on retirement.
3. **Tolerant checks during transition.** The `cer/*` checks accept both the old thin-stub shape and the new vendored shape until the migration retires, so no consumer's check suite goes red mid-flight.
4. **Docs.** Update `RELEASE.md`, `.github/workflows/README.md` (drop the frozen-`@main`-API section), and the pack fingerprint.

## Prerequisite for the automatic cut

The automatic phase-2 deletion needs `FLEET_GITHUB_TOKEN` granted **Contents-write on the home repo** — #239 notes this is not granted yet. Until it is, the census logs "grant FLEET_GITHUB_TOKEN Contents write" and Claudinite's copies stay in place (harmless — consumers already run off their vendored copies by then).

Refs #270 (RELEASE item), #239 (token scope).","state":"open","html_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/276","user":{"login":"missingbulb","id":73882448,"profile_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/73882448?v=4"},"author_association":"OWNER","labels":["blocked"],"assignees":[],"comments":5,"reactions":{"total_count":0,"+1":0,"-1":0,"laugh":0,"confused":0,"heart":0,"hooray":0,"rocket":0,"eyes":0},"created_at":"2026-07-13T14:28:14Z","updated_at":"2026-08-22T05:13:24Z","has_parent":false,"has_children":false,"closed_by_pull_requests":{"total_count":0,"references":[]}}

{"number":170,"title":"Revisit: Workflow tool's interactive opt-in blocks unattended routines (waiting on Anthropic)","body":"## The limitation

The multi-agent-orchestration **`Workflow`** tool requires an **interactive human opt-in on every run** ("Allow Claude to run a workflow?"). That prompt only disappears under bypass-permissions / headless modes a scheduler can't be relied on to be in. Because an unattended routine has no human to click **Allow**, any routine that fans out through the Workflow tool stalls on step one.

This also means the tool's nicest ergonomics are off-limits to us for unattended work: committing a Workflow script and having the nightly job just run it by name (`Workflow({name: ...})`) hits the **same** prompt — the gate is on *invoking* a workflow, not on authoring one. And the parallel-agent step can't be pushed into a plain committed script either, since spawning Claude subagents is a harness capability, not something arbitrary code can call.

## Our current workaround

We fan the fleet daily maintenance routine out with **plain subagent dispatch** (the Agent/Task tool) instead, which carries no opt-in gate, and the orchestrator honors the phase barriers itself. See #168 / #169 and `routines/auto-all-repos-maintenance.md` + `skills/unattended-agents/SKILL.md`.

This works and is the right default (no dependency on an out-of-repo permission-mode setting), but it costs us the Workflow tool's built-in phase/barrier machinery and the option to run committed, reviewed orchestration code.

## Why keep this open

This is a limitation of the platform, not our code — we're **waiting on the world to change**. If Anthropic later lets an unattended session pre-authorize the Workflow tool (a settings allowlist entry, an environment/routine permission mode that reliably suppresses just this prompt, or persisted per-workflow consent that survives a fresh cloud clone), we could reconsider using committed Workflow scripts for the fleet routine and get determinism + review back.

**Action:** periodically check with Anthropic / the Claude Code release notes whether the Workflow tool can be pre-authorized for unattended sessions. When it can, revisit the plain-dispatch decision in the routine spec.

{"number":1133,"title":"converge-item.mjs needs a real GITHUB_TOKEN the queue's own sessions don't have","body":"`engine/scheduler/queue/instructions.md` step 6 tells every work-item session to converge by running:

```bash
node /scheduler/queue/converge-item.mjs --issue  --outcome ... --summary '...'
```

`converge-item.mjs` reads and writes the issue over a direct `api.github.com` fetch, authenticated with `process.env.GITHUB_TOKEN` (`engine/scheduler/signals/gh.mjs`). That's fine for the retired executor mechanism, which ran as the Action's own job step with `GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}` set in its shell (`.github/workflows/claudinite-executor.yml`). But the sessions the *current* queue dispatches to are Claude Code cloud/web sessions (`claude.ai/code/session_...`, per the hand-off comment on each work item) — and that session type's platform policy is MCP-only GitHub access: no `gh` CLI, no direct API calls. The `GITHUB_TOKEN` such a session does see in its shell env is not a GitHub credential at all (14 chars, `prox...` prefix — a proxy artifact), so the script's very first call (`readIssue`) fails with a 401 before it ever reaches its own judgment logic.

Hit this converging #1129 (implementing #1124): `GITHUB_REPOSITORY=missingbulb/Claudinite node engine/scheduler/queue/converge-item.mjs --issue 1129 --outcome done --summary '...'` exited 1 with `converge-item: #1129 could not be read`. Worked around it by replicating the script's side effects (comment with the same `claudinite-task-exec` record line, `task:agent`→`task:done` swap, close as completed) directly over the `mcp__github__*` tools instead — same end state, just not "in code" as instructed. Skipped only the `readyDependents` release, which `readiness.mjs` itself documents as safe to skip for a close performed outside the script (the hourly scheduler run is the backstop).

The retired `executor.md` already solved the same problem for a different script shape: its `needs-issue` verdict has the session fetch the one issue it needs over MCP, save the raw JSON, and hand it to the shell via `--issue-json ` rather than have the shell fetch it itself. `converge-item.mjs` has no such path — it only ever fetches and writes live. Given it writes too (comment, label, close), an `--issue-json` equivalent alone wouldn't fully solve it; it'd need either a write-side MCP shim as well, or a documented "no working token → do these exact steps over your GitHub tools instead" fallback in `instructions.md` step 6, mirroring what every session hitting this will otherwise rediscover from scratch.

Every future `implement-request` (and any other queue task converging through this same step 6) will hit this identically in this session type — this isn't specific to #1124/#1129.","state":"open","html_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1133","user":{"login":"missingbulb","id":73882448,"profile_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/73882448?v=4"},"author_association":"OWNER","labels":["quick-win"],"assignees":[],"comments":3,"reactions":{"total_count":0,"+1":0,"-1":0,"laugh":0,"confused":0,"heart":0,"hooray":0,"rocket":0,"eyes":0},"created_at":"2026-08-20T22:03:49Z","updated_at":"2026-08-22T05:12:13Z","has_parent":false,"has_children":false,"closed_by_pull_requests":{"total_count":0,"references":[]}}

Base directory for this skill: /home/user/Claudinite/.claude/skills/single-issue-triage

# Single-issue triage

Triage **one** open issue and take the **first** applicable action. This **acts** — but every action
defaults to the reversible option when the check is inconclusive.

- **Already implemented in `main`** → **close** (`completed`) + a one-line comment citing where it
  landed.
- **Conflicts with a current guideline** → label `needs-decision` + a comment naming the conflict.
- **Blocked by another issue** → label `blocked` + a comment `blocked by #N`.
- **Small and quick to do** → label `quick-win` + a comment scoping it.
- **Else** → leave it.

**Every checkbox in the issue body ticked** is the author's own claim that the work is done — the
strongest completion signal an issue can carry, and the one thing that puts an otherwise quiet issue
into the first rung. It is **a claim, not proof**: read it as a reason to run the implemented-in-`main`
check, never as the answer. Verified ⇒ close; not ⇒ comment naming what is still missing. A
partially-ticked list is not a completion signal at all — triage the issue as if it carried no boxes.
Where the ask has **no repo-side artifact** (a console setting, a routine only a human can touch), those
ticks by the issue's own author are the closing condition — say so and close.

**"Implemented in `main`" means the issue's actual ask is true of `main`'s content _now_** — confirm
it there and cite it. **Never** infer it from a linked PR merging or the issue merely looking done. If
you can't point to it, **comment, don't close.** Create a label if it's missing. Return `{ action,
note }` (action one of closed/needs-decision/blocked/quick-win/left/unchanged).

## Never re-post a verdict you already posted

A triage comment updates the issue, and an updated issue is the next window's touched-issue
trigger — so a comment that only restates the last one wakes this task again tomorrow, and again
the day after. The verdict is the news; re-deriving it is not.

Before writing anything, read the issue's comments and find the most recent one this task posted
— by its marker, or, on an issue triaged before the marker existed, by its wording. If the action
you are about to take is the one that comment already announced, **post nothing and change nothing**
(a label already on the issue included) and return `{ action: 'unchanged', note: '<action> since
<its date>' }`. Closing is never a repeat: it changes the issue's state and ends the sequence.

End every comment you post with this marker, alone on the last line:

```
<!-- claudinite:tidy-issues verdict=<action> -->
```

{"number":1119,"title":"Migrate to the unified task:status:/task:origin: label scheme","body":"Tracking issue for the label-scheme migration. The end state and its rationale: `docs/label-scheme/DESIGN.md` (lands in #1120). This body is the plan — phases sorted by what blocks; append-only once implementation starts.

## Phase 0 — out-of-band setup

- [x] None needed — confirmed: labels are created by the engine's ensure-if-missing pass with the Action's own `GITHUB_TOKEN`, and the stubs already declare `issues: write`. No secret, grant, or platform setting changes.

## Review pass — one stacked-PR arrival, base-first on #1120

- [ ] **PR 1 — read side + stubs** (additive, safe on every member in any order): the one-pass decode map (every legacy spelling → canonical status), new label constants and ensure-list entries, and the scheduler/executor stubs — canon's own `.github/workflows/` copies in the same commit — triggering on legacy *and* new ready/urgent spellings and filing failure issues as `task:origin:github` + `task:status:needs-human-failure`. Nothing writes a new label yet. Exit: merged, suite green against current `main`.
- [ ] **PR 2 — one-issue request mode**: adoption reads `task:origin:ad-hoc`-with-no-status beside `claude-task`, writes the machine block onto the marked issue, gates body parameters on the author's push access (collaborators-permission API), and the `Task:` targeting field lands with `add-packs` folded into it. Still writes legacy status spellings. Exit: merged.
- [ ] **PR 3 — write-side flip**: constants' values change to the new spellings (statuses; origins — generator writes `planned`, adoption `ad-hoc`, stubs `github`), janitor and dashboard follow, `claude-*` writes retire. Exit: merged — merge is gated on execution step 1 below.
- [ ] **PR 4 — ride-alongs**: product-wiki's gate reads its own approval-parked item instead of a labeled PR; vocabulary sweep over docs and check catalogs. Exit: merged.

## Execution — no human gate after the review pass

- [ ] After PRs 1–2 merge: force `fleet-baseline` with `follow` and watch to a terminal state (a stub-contract change must work on every member — the nightly is not the delivery). Exit: every member's executor workflow at HEAD triggers on both ready/urgent spellings, read from each repo's file and judged by stamps, never run conclusions. If stubs prove to be copied-once rather than converge-delivered, stop here and route the stub change through the drift lane before PR 3 merges.
- [ ] Merge PRs 3–4; force the fleet again; watch to terminal state. Exit: a fresh scheduler cycle on a real member files items wearing only new spellings, and open pre-scheme items still decode and drain.
- [ ] Open items are not mass-relabeled; each converges under the decode map, and the janitor writes canonical labels when repairing a torn one. Exit: no open item fleet-wide wears a legacy state spelling.

## Tail — destructive, only after the cutover is observed

- [ ] Remove legacy spellings from the stub triggers once no fielded engine writes them (read members' vendored engine versions, not the calendar).
- [ ] Mark legacy label series historical wherever counts are folded. {"number":1169,"title":"Dissolve docs/skill-usage-metrics/DESIGN.md into the packs that own its subjects","body":"The owner's read, and it holds up against the tree: this design doc collapses into the pack that collects the signals and into the dashboard. It is 769 lines describing a pipeline that is now built, and the canon's own rule for that is already written — *behaviour belongs in the module header and the pack README*, not in a doc that has to be kept in step with both.

The evidence, section by section (line counts from `2026-08-21`):

| § | Lines | Where it already lives, or should |
|---|---|---|
| 1 Where knowledge lives | 16 | A standing architectural rule ("the canon knows mechanisms, never repos") — belongs with the local pack's standing decisions, not in one initiative's doc |
| 2 Sources of truth | 18 | `claudinite-growth/README.md` |
| 3 Capture (3.1–3.5) | ~100 | `claudinite-growth/README.md` already carries the capture lifecycle and retention almost verbatim; `capture-log.mjs`'s header carries the rest. **§3.4 (capturing an unattended session, where no SessionEnd hook fires) and §3.5 (the ordering constraint) are the one part with no other home** — they go into the pack README beside the lifecycle they belong to |
| 4.1 Check activations | 101 | Duplicated: `usage-fold/README.md`'s "The check failures are the win" and `fold-usage.mjs`'s header both carry the three marks, the CI-in-the-loop rule and the floor property |
| 4.2 Task invocations | 69 | Describes the retired slot-scheduler census. Keep two sentences of it as history in `usage-fold/README.md` (which already has them) and drop the rest |
| 4.3 Exec statuses | 16 | `usage-fold/README.md` |
| 5 The per-repo aggregate + shape | 146 | Duplicated: `usage-fold/README.md` and `usage-format.mjs`'s header |
| 6 The fleet aggregate | 63 | Superseded; **deleted outright** — the task it describes goes in #1166 |
| 7 Consumers | 40 | Split: the promotion-ladder half to `claudinite-growth/README.md`, the reader half to `claudinite-dashboard/README.md` |
| 8 TTLs | 12 | `claudinite-growth/README.md` (it already states retention) |
| 9 Failure modes | 45 | Duplicated: `usage-fold/README.md`'s "Failure is visible, never silent" |
| 10 + the two later rounds | 57 | Owner decisions with their rationale. These are the doc's only irreplaceable content — move them to the local pack's standing decisions, where a session actually reads them |

So the shape of the change: **almost nothing is written fresh.** Two sections move (§3.4/§3.5, and the decision record), one is deleted, and the rest is verified as already-covered and then dropped. If a section turns out *not* to be covered where this table claims, write it into the pack — do not keep the doc alive for it.

## The references are the real work

Eight files point into this doc by section number, and a dangling `§` pointer is worse than no pointer:

```
engine/hooks/session-end-command.mjs          §3.3
engine/scheduler/run-record.mjs               §4.2
packs/claudinite-growth/session-end.mjs       (unnumbered)
packs/claudinite-growth/tasks/usage-fold/task.mjs        §5
packs/claudinite-growth/tasks/usage-fold/worker.mjs      §5
packs/claudinite-growth/tasks/usage-fold/fold-usage.mjs  §4, §5
docs/per-project-scheduling/DESIGN.md         §4.2 and one unnumbered
```

Each becomes either a pointer to the pack README section that absorbed it, or — better where the sentence was only citing itself — nothing at all. Use the `repo-text-sweeps` skill; grep for `skill-usage-metrics` afterwards and confirm zero hits outside history.

## Done looks like

**Done looks like**: a member's converge removes `.claudinite/shared/packs//` for each absorbed pack, and a member that already converged past the record still gets there. Confirm against a real member tree, not only a fixture — the same way #1186 was confirmed.

input.prompt:
You are triaging GitHub issues in repo missingbulb/Claudinite as part of the `tidy-issues` maintenance task. Use ONLY the mcp__github__* MCP tools for GitHub access (issue_read, issue_write, add_issue_comment, get_label, list_issue_fields). You also have local repo access at /home/user/Claudinite (already `git fetch origin main`-ed; origin/main tip is e26e0c188fbd7b11c702babc89d4014bda1f4716) via Bash/Grep/Read — use `git show origin/main:<path>` or `git grep <pattern> origin/main -- <path>` to check what's actually true of main's CURRENT content. Do not check out or modify any branch; read-only against origin/main.

Triage EACH of these issue numbers, one at a time, independently: 1112, 1113, 1106, 1073, 748, 722, 1072, 1010, 1078, 394

## The triage ladder — take the FIRST applicable action per issue

1. **Already implemented in `main`** → verify the issue's actual ask is true of origin/main's content NOW (never infer from a linked PR merging or the issue "looking" done) → **close** it (issue_write: state=closed, state_reason=completed) + post a one-line comment citing exactly where/how it's true in main (file/behavior), ending with the marker below.
2. **Conflicts with a current guideline/rule in the repo** (e.g. contradicts something in CLAUDE.md / packs/*/RULES.md as currently written) → apply label `needs-decision` (get current labels first — see label-safety note below) + comment naming the conflict, ending with the marker.
3. **Blocked by another issue** (that other issue is open and must land first) → apply label `blocked` + comment `blocked by #N`, ending with the marker.
4. **Small and quick to do** (a well-scoped, low-risk change) → apply label `quick-win` + comment scoping what the quick fix is, ending with the marker.
5. **Else** → leave it untouched. Take no action, post nothing.

### Checkbox signal
If EVERY checkbox in the issue body is ticked, that's the author's own claim of completion — a reason to run the "implemented in main" check (rung 1), never proof by itself. Verified true in main ⇒ close citing where. Not verified ⇒ comment naming what's still missing (this IS an action — it's a comment, so log it, but do NOT close). A partially-ticked list is not a completion signal at all — triage as if no boxes existed. If the ask has NO repo-side artifact (e.g., a console/platform setting only a human can touch), the author's own ticks are the closing condition — say so in your comment and close.

### Never re-post a verdict already posted
Before doing anything, read the issue's existing comments (issue_read method=get_comments). Find the most recent comment ending in a `<!-- claudinite:tidy-issues verdict=... -->` marker (or, for an issue triaged before the marker existed, one that clearly restates this same verdict in wording). If the action you're about to take is the SAME action that comment already announced, take NO action and NO comment — record this issue's outcome as `unchanged` (note: "<action> since <date>"). Closing is never a repeat — it changes the issue's actual state, so if the issue is still open and your verdict is "close", always execute the close even if a prior comment argued for it.

### Marker
End every comment you post (whether it's a close comment, needs-decision, blocked, quick-win, or a "still missing" comment) with this exact line alone at the end:
```
<!-- claudinite:tidy-issues verdict=<action> -->
```
where `<action>` is one of: closed, needs-decision, blocked, quick-win (use `closed` even for the "still missing, not closing" case is WRONG — for that case, since you did NOT close, there is no verdict action from the ladder; skip posting a marker-bearing comment for that sub-case only if you're unsure, but generally: if you post a comment about missing work under the checkbox path without closing, treat it as a regular open triage note and do not apply a verdict marker since it isn't a ladder outcome — just leave it uncommented in that edge case and record it as `left`).

### Label safety
GitHub's issue-update label field REPLACES the full label set, it doesn't add to it. Before applying `needs-decision`/`blocked`/`quick-win`, call issue_read method=get_labels to get the issue's CURRENT labels, then call issue_write method=update with labels = (existing labels ∪ {new label}), deduplicated. If get_label shows the label doesn't exist in the repo yet, still include it in the issue_write labels array (GitHub auto-creates on issue update in most configs); if the write errors, note the failure in your report but still post the comment (the comment is the actual triage signal).

## What NOT to do
- Never touch PRs, branches, or push code. Never comment on or close a PR even if a number here happens to be one (check first: issue_read get gets you `pull_request`-shaped data if it's actually a PR — if so, skip it and note "is a PR, not an issue, skipped").
- Never invent implementation status — cite exact file paths / content from origin/main.
- Don't over-post: if uncertain, prefer "left" over guessing.

## Output format
When done with all 10 issues, report back a plain list, one line per issue, EXACTLY in this format:
`#<number>: <action> — <one-sentence note>`
where `<action>` is one of: closed, needs-decision, blocked, quick-win, left, unchanged, skipped-pr.
This is your entire deliverable — return just this list (10 lines), nothing else.

4. **Small and quick to do** (a well-scoped, low-risk change) → apply label `quick-win` + comment scoping what the quick fix is, ending with the marker.
5. **Else** → leave it untouched. Take no action, post nothing.

### Checkbox signal
If EVERY checkbox in the issue body is ticked, that's the author's own claim of completion — a reason to run the "implemented in main" check (rung 1), never proof by itself. Verified true in main ⇒ close citing where. Not verified ⇒ comment naming what's still missing (this IS an action — it's a comment, so log it, but do NOT close). A partially-ticked list is not a completion signal at all — triage as if no boxes existed. If the ask has NO repo-side artifact (e.g., a console/platform setting only a human can touch), the author's own ticks are the closing condition — say so in your comment and close.

### Never re-post a verdict already posted
Before doing anything, read the issue's existing comments (issue_read method=get_comments). Find the most recent comment ending in a `<!-- claudinite:tidy-issues verdict=... -->` marker (or, for an issue triaged before the marker existed, one that clearly restates this same verdict in wording). If the action you're about to take is the SAME action that comment already announced, take NO action and NO comment — record this issue's outcome as `unchanged` (note: "<action> since <date>"). Closing is never a repeat — it changes the issue's actual state, so if the issue is still open and your verdict is "close", always execute the close even if a prior comment argued for it.

### Marker
End every comment you post (whether it's a close comment, needs-decision, blocked, quick-win, or a "still missing" comment) with this exact line alone at the end:
```
<!-- claudinite:tidy-issues verdict=<action> -->
```
where `<action>` is one of: closed, needs-decision, blocked, quick-win (use `closed` even for the "still missing, not closing" case is WRONG — for that case, since you did NOT close, there is no verdict action from the ladder; skip posting a marker-bearing comment for that sub-case only if you're unsure, but generally: if you post a comment about missing work under the checkbox path without closing, treat it as a regular open triage note and do not apply a verdict marker since it isn't a ladder outcome — just leave it uncommented in that edge case and record it as `left`).

### Label safety
GitHub's issue-update label field REPLACES the full label set, it doesn't add to it. Before applying `needs-decision`/`blocked`/`quick-win`, call issue_read method=get_labels to get the issue's CURRENT labels, then call issue_write method=update with labels = (existing labels ∪ {new label}), deduplicated. If get_label shows the label doesn't exist in the repo yet, still include it in the issue_write labels array (GitHub auto-creates on issue update in most configs); if the write errors, note the failure in your report but still post the comment (the comment is the actual triage signal).

## What NOT to do
- Never touch PRs, branches, or push code. Never comment on or close a PR even if a number here happens to be one (check first: issue_read get gets you `pull_request`-shaped data if it's actually a PR — if so, skip it and note "is a PR, not an issue, skipped").
- Never invent implementation status — cite exact file paths / content from origin/main.
- Don't over-post: if uncertain, prefer "left" over guessing.

## Output format
When done with all 10 issues, report back a plain list, one line per issue, EXACTLY in this format:
`#<number>: <action> — <one-sentence note>`
where `<action>` is one of: closed, needs-decision, blocked, quick-win, left, unchanged, skipped-pr.
This is your entire deliverable — return just this list (10 lines), nothing else.

```
! could not reconcile label "claude-automerge": 404
```

Seen on `main`'s run [32368276774](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/actions/runs/32368276774/job/96422660810) and on a branch run of #1089 at the same minute, so it is **not** from that PR — it is standing behavior on every run, and has been long enough that nobody reads the line any more.

`ensureLabels(gh, repo, [...QUEUE_LABELS, ...REQUEST_LABELS])` is the caller; `AUTOMERGE_LABEL` (`claude-automerge`) is in `REQUEST_LABELS`. The reconcile is fail-soft, which is why the run stays green — but the label is the asker's merge authorization (`MERGE_IF_NARROW`), read from a write-gated label at adoption. A label that cannot be reconciled is one that may not exist in the picker for a person to apply, which would make that authorization unreachable rather than merely unstamped.

Worth establishing before deciding the fix:

- whether the label exists on the repo at all, or the 404 is the *update* path failing on a label that does exist,
- whether the same line appears on members (it would be the same code, so probably),
- whether anything has ever successfully read `claude-automerge` off an issue here.

# Single-issue triage

Triage **one** open issue and take the **first** applicable action. This **acts** — but every action
defaults to the reversible option when the check is inconclusive.

- **Already implemented in `main`** → **close** (`completed`) + a one-line comment citing where it
  landed.
- **Conflicts with a current guideline** → label `needs-decision` + a comment naming the conflict.
- **Blocked by another issue** → label `blocked` + a comment `blocked by #N`.
- **Small and quick to do** → label `quick-win` + a comment scoping it.
- **Else** → leave it.

**Every checkbox in the issue body ticked** is the author's own claim that the work is done — the
strongest completion signal an issue can carry, and the one thing that puts an otherwise quiet issue
into the first rung. It is **a claim, not proof**: read it as a reason to run the implemented-in-`main`
check, never as the answer. Verified ⇒ close; not ⇒ comment naming what is still missing. A
partially-ticked list is not a completion signal at all — triage the issue as if it carried no boxes.
Where the ask has **no repo-side artifact** (a console setting, a routine only a human can touch), those
ticks by the issue's own author are the closing condition — say so and close.

**"Implemented in `main`" means the issue's actual ask is true of `main`'s content _now_** — confirm
it there and cite it. **Never** infer it from a linked PR merging or the issue merely looking done. If
you can't point to it, **comment, don't close.** Create a label if it's missing. Return `{ action,
note }` (action one of closed/needs-decision/blocked/quick-win/left/unchanged).

## Never re-post a verdict you already posted

A triage comment updates the issue, and an updated issue is the next window's touched-issue
trigger — so a comment that only restates the last one wakes this task again tomorrow, and again
the day after. The verdict is the news; re-deriving it is not.

Before writing anything, read the issue's comments and find the most recent one this task posted
— by its marker, or, on an issue triaged before the marker existed, by its wording. If the action
you are about to take is the one that comment already announced, **post nothing and change nothing**
(a label already on the issue included) and return `{ action: 'unchanged', note: '<action> since
<its date>' }`. Closing is never a repeat: it changes the issue's state and ends the sequence.

End every comment you post with this marker, alone on the last line:

```
<!-- claudinite:tidy-issues verdict=<action> -->
```

{"number":1112,"title":"Verify in production: a member's un-converged workflow still starts a scheduler run through the `tick.mjs` shim","body":"#877 renamed `engine/scheduler/queue/tick.mjs` to `scheduler-run.mjs` and left a shim at the old path (DESIGN decision 27, landed in #1108 / `a9a783e`).

**Why this could not be watched now.** The two halves of the change reach a member on different clocks. The mount refreshes on a converge; `.github/workflows/claudinite-scheduler.yml` is the one path a converge cannot push, so it lands later as a pull request somebody merges. The window this shim exists for — **new mount, old workflow, still naming `tick.mjs`** — therefore only opens once a member has converged, and is only exercised at that member's next hourly scheduler run. At the time of writing GoogleCalendarEventCreator had the old mount and the old workflow, so the window had not opened yet.

A synthetic version of it is already covered: the `old-workflows` rehearsal fixture converges a member holding the previous workflow shape, and `engine-tests/scheduler/queue/scheduler-run-entry-shim.test.mjs` pins that the shim starts the run and that `scheduler-workflow-shape` accepts either spelling. What no test can show is a real member's scheduler workflow running green through it.

If this fails, every member in that window has a queue that has silently stopped — nothing instantiates standing items, nothing readies blocked ones, nothing reclaims a dead claim — with no run left to report it.

In-production-when: any member repo whose `.claudinite/shared/engine/scheduler/queue/scheduler-run.mjs` exists AND whose `.github/workflows/claudinite-scheduler.yml` still runs `queue/tick.mjs`. A pass is that line plus a green conclusion. A failure is any conclusion other than `success`, or a run whose log shows the entry point could not be found.

Keep `parseVersion`'s treatment of **zero** — that is the install floor (`docs/versioned-updates/DESIGN.md` §3), not a legacy version.

## 1. A structural block: promote's ladder cannot reach the check rung

`growth-promote`'s task spec says a lesson a check can carry is **authored as the check** in the promote PR — "the rule module in the right pack, the failure message carrying the generalized lesson, **plus a fixture test proving it fires**".

That is mechanically impossible today:

- promote's write surface is bounded to `packs/` and `skills/`, enforced by `.claudinite/local/packs/canon-curation/promote-scope.mjs` on the `growth-promote` branch prefix;
- a canon pack's fixture test lives under `packs-tests/`, which is **outside** that surface;
- and it cannot move into `packs/` either — `.github/workflows/ci.yml` pins a closed set of test roots (`engine-tests/`, `packs-tests/`, `vendoring/`, `dev/tools/`, `.claudinite/local/packs/`), with `engine-tests/ci-test-roots.test.mjs` failing on any tracked test outside them.

So every promote run must fall back to prose for a convertible rule, and the "prose is the fallback, not the default" ladder never fires. Whichever way it is resolved (widen `inBounds` to `packs-tests/`, or add `packs/` as a test root), it is an owner decision — the run declined to widen its own gate.

## 2. The conversion this blocked

The `.gitignore`-pruning lesson (LaughCounter's local pack, promoted as prose to `git-github-advanced` in #747) converts to a world-scope `basics` check. Written and green locally before being pulled:

- **`packs/basics/committed-build-artifact.mjs`** — advisory, relevance-first. Flags a *tracked* file matching a confined set of artifacts no project tracks on purpose: `__pycache__/`, `*.py[co]`, `.pytest_cache/`, `.mypy_cache/`, `.ruff_cache/`, `*.egg-info/`, `.DS_Store`, `Thumbs.db`. The `fix` line carries the lesson (delete the artifacts before dropping their ignore rules; read `git diff --cached --stat` after a bulk `git add -A`).
- **`packs-tests/basics/committed-build-artifact.test.mjs`** — four cases: clean tree silent; a swept-in `__pycache__` found; the tool-cache/OS set found; and a narrowness case proving silence on deliberately vendored trees (`node_modules/`, `dist/`, `build/`) and on prose merely naming `__pycache__`.

Advisory rather than blocking on purpose: the fix is a deletion, and pre-existing junk in a member repo should surface as a finding to clear, not red that repo's sweep and block its maintenance PR.

The set was chosen so the check stays inert on anything a repo might legitimately vendor; `node_modules/` and `dist/` are deliberately excluded.

{"number":1073,"title":"Move the Chrome Web Store release pipeline into Claudinite tasks","body":"Tracking issue. The `chrome-extension` pack ships the store release as five workflows plus three composite actions, with a `store-release` task that only *dispatches* them. Move the work itself into task code-work.

> ### ⛔ Blocked on #883
>
> **Do not start implementing anything.** #883 changes the queue-engine contract this plan is written against. Phase -1 below must complete first, and the revised plan needs owner approval before any code is written.

> **Body repaired 2026-08-20**, before any implementation, per `writing-migration-plans`. The original is archived in a comment below; the comment trail holds the derivation and the review that forced these changes. **From the first commit onward this body is append-only.**

Follows #1069 / #1071, which established that the grounds for keeping a workflow are narrower than the corpus claimed: an Actions-only secret is reachable from code-work (`required_secrets`), an OIDC identity is a `permissions:` line, and a one-shot external effect is `on_interrupt: 'needs-human'`. The only surviving ground is the Actions **composition model** — a `uses:` step. In this pipeline that is exactly and only the Pages deploy.

## Owner decisions

1. **The privacy-page refresh leaves the release path.** It renders `PRIVACY.md`, which changes on its own schedule, not on every store publish. It gets its own trigger — and that is what removes the last `uses:` from the release path.
2. **Human "bump version" merges stay manual.** Today a bump merge cuts the GitHub Release but does **not** upload to the store; a human publishes deliberately. The daily patch auto-release remains the only automatic path to the store.
3. **`store-publish` reads the store** to decide whether the latest release is live, rather than inferring from the version diff.
4. **Member cleanup is done by a session** (route c). The general "no automation can retire a workflow it once delivered" gap stays unfiled; no pre-flight push.
5. **The bump lands as a self-merging PR**, not a push to main — via `engine/scheduler/deliver-generated.mjs` → `land-pr.mjs`, under the member's own `maintenance.delivery`.

## End state — three atoms, plus the privacy page

One operation per task, chained by preconditions rather than by ordering edges or parameters. Each precondition becomes true *because the previous task produced its output*.

| task | frequency | precondition | does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `release-patch-bump` | daily | shipped paths changed since the latest release tag | patch bump, landed as a self-merging PR |
| `release-package` | manual | manifest version ahead of the latest release | build + cut the GitHub Release |
| `store-publish` | manual | the latest release is not live on the store | upload the prod zip |
| `privacy-page` | manual | `PRIVACY.md` touched, or woken | dispatch the Pages deploy |

The `manual` tasks are woken by the session that merges the bump PR — "bump version" lands via a normal PR and `LGTM` merges it in-session, so a witness is already present and no cadence is needed.

`on_interrupt: 'needs-human'` belongs on **`store-publish` alone** — the store upload is the one genuinely non-idempotent act. The decomposition makes every other stage self-healing: a torn run leaves the world in a state the next stage's precondition re-derives.

`expected_outcome: 'merged-pr'` on `release-patch-bump`. `required_secrets: ['CHROME_EXTENSION_ID', 'CHROME_CLIENT_ID', 'CHROME_CLIENT_SECRET', 'CHROME_REFRESH_TOKEN']` on `store-publish`.

### What each piece becomes

| today | becomes |
|---|---|
| `chrome-extension-release.yml` (orchestrator) | deleted — the tasks own every trigger |
| `chrome-extension-daily-release.yml` | split across the three atoms |
| `chrome-extension-create-package.yml` | `release-package`'s worker |
| `chrome-extension-publish-store.yml` | `store-publish`'s worker |
| `deploy-privacy-page.yml` | survives, rewritten to be dispatchable; the one remaining `uses:` surface |
| `actions/read-release-config/`, `actions/bump-extension-patch/` | plain modules the workers import; the `action.yml` wrappers deleted |
| `actions/report-failure/` | deleted, with **no replacement** — a failing task parks `needs-human`, which is the error report |
| `release-workflows.mjs` conformance | mostly deleted; what remains guards `release.config`, not workflow shape |

## Phase -1 — revisit against #883 (blocking)

#883 implements the work-as-work amendments in `engine/scheduler/queue/`. Several of this plan's conclusions were reasoned against the pre-amendment contract and must be re-derived, not merely re-read.

- [ ] **Re-derive the leash conclusion.** The plan concluded "no split; `release-package` stays one task" from a 50-minute job budget shared across `maxItems` items. #883 retires `timeout-minutes ≤ leash` once heartbeat comments land, and re-sizes run timeouts to `maxItems` × the largest work bound. Long work stops being illegal, so the constraint that produced that conclusion no longer exists in the same form.
- [ ] **Re-derive the chain's latency.** The three atoms are chained by preconditions, each becoming true because the previous produced its output. Under today's engine each link waits a tick (~1h). #883's **self-re-dispatch** and **readiness re-check at close (F1)** are both aimed exactly at that — with them, the chain drains in one sitting. This changes whether the decomposition is cheap or expensive, and may change the `frequency` choices.
- [ ] **Re-check the `report-failure` deletion against the durable record.** #883 adds the `claudinite-task-exec` record plus artifact links to the terminal comment, noting that today *"an agentless run's only record expires with its Actions log."* All three release tasks are agentless. Confirm the park-plus-record is the whole replacement, since the deletion was decided before that record existed.
- [ ] **Account for the `prework` → work-step key rename.** #883 lists it as a fleet migration touching the vendored key in every member's task files, shipped with a compatibility window. Writing three new task declarations immediately before that rename means authoring them on vocabulary that is about to change; decide whether to wait, or to write them on the new key behind the compatibility window.
- [ ] **Re-check tick/drain decoupling against Phase 2.** The drain leaving the tick's concurrency group changes how a forced `wake` behaves during member verification.
- [ ] **Re-run the whole plan review** (the `writing-migration-plans` findings-by-cost sort) against the amended engine, then **get owner approval on the revised plan before any code is written.**

**Exit:** #883 closed, every box above answered in a comment on this issue, and the owner has approved the revised plan.

## Phase 0 — out-of-band setup

**Nothing outside the repo.** The four `CHROME_*` secrets already exist in member repos under these names; no new token grant (the executor already has `contents: write` and `actions: write`); Pages source unchanged.

There **is** a delivery dependency, but it is a Phase 2 entry condition rather than a human step — see Phase 2.

## Phase 1 — the PR stack (one review gate)

PRs 1–4 stacked, each based on the previous, reviewed together, merged base-first. **PR 5 is authored in the stack but held out of that merge** — it is destructive to the canon's own delivery surface, so it lands only after Phase 2 reads back true.

- [ ] **1. Two signal collectors, and `release.config` as a module.** Lift `read-config.mjs` out of the composite action. Add to the `release` collector: a `/compare/{latestTag}...{defaultBranch}` changed-files read, and a store live-version read. Both are required — a precondition receives only `(signals, packConfig)` (`engine/scheduler/queue/executor.mjs:326-328`) and the scheduler's checkout is depth-1 with no tags (`claudinite-scheduler.yml:56`), so neither answer is otherwise reachable. **Try the unauthenticated store read first**; only if it is unstable do credentials enter the signal layer, and then via `ctx` (the `signals/local.mjs` shape), never `process.env` inside a collector.
- [ ] **2. The three task declarations,** with authoritative preconditions over those signals.
- [ ] **3. The three workers.** `release-patch-bump` writes through `deliver-generated.mjs` — nothing touches the drain's checkout.
- [ ] **4. `privacy-page`, and `deploy-privacy-page.yml` rewritten** — add `workflow_dispatch`, carry its own `permissions:`, drop the `./.github/actions/report-failure` reference (Phase 3 deletes that composite).
- [ ] **5. (held) Retire the pack's workflow surface** — the four stubs, the composite actions, the `release-workflows.mjs` conformance, and the canon's own orphaned `.github/workflows/chrome-extension-*.yml` copies.

**Exit (PRs 1–4):** `node --test $(git ls-files '*.test.mjs')` green on `main`, and the four task declarations validate against `engine/scheduler/task-contract.mjs`.

## Phase 2 — execution

- [ ] **Entry condition:** each member's executor carries the four `CHROME_*` names under `# claudinite:secrets`. The stamp edits `.github/workflows/claudinite-executor.yml`, which `GITHUB_TOKEN` cannot write, so it travels the withhold lane and lands via an apply-stage session. Without this the first forced run parks "missing secrets" and reads like a failure.
- [ ] Drive the pipeline on `missingbulb/GoogleCalendarEventCreator`, waking each atom in turn.
      **Exit:** each task's item terminal, and the store shows a submission at the expected version.
- [ ] Repeat on `TLDR` and `CrosswordChat`.
      **Exit:** all three members' items terminal.

## Phase 3 — the tail (destructive; only after Phase 2 reads back true)

- [ ] Merge PR 5.
- [ ] Attach the three member repos to a session with push access; delete the four `chrome-extension-*` workflows and the three `.github/actions/` composites from each, one PR per repo.
      **Exit:** each member's `.github/workflows/` contains `deploy-privacy-page.yml` and no other `chrome-extension-*` file, and each member's next release item still converges terminal.

A straggler between Phases 2 and 3 is **benign**: a leftover orchestrator's `create-package`-on-push does exactly what `release-package` does, and it no-ops when the version is already released. Whichever runs first cuts the Release; the other declines.

## Risks

- **`readShipsReleasePipeline`** detects a publisher by the orchestrator's `name:` **or** `.github/release.config`. Deleting the orchestrator leaves the config as the only signal; exercise that fallback before Phase 3, not during it.
- **Latency.** The daily patch release is unchanged. A human bump's Release waits for a deliberate wake — which is decision 2, not a regression. {"number":1072,"title":"Production code must not reference its tests — land it as a check","body":"Owner decision while landing #1066: **there shouldn't be references to tests from production code.** That change removed the four citations it created; the rule itself is still unwritten, and eleven pre-existing sites still cross the line.

## The rule

A shipping `.mjs` under `packs/` or `engine/` must not name a `*.test.mjs` path. It is deterministic, so it belongs on the ladder as a **check**, not prose — the assurance authored and seen to fail before the sites are cleaned.

Documentation is a separate question and probably outside it: `engine/checks/README.md` describing where a pack's tests live, or `.github/workflows/ci.yml` naming test globs, is the corpus documenting itself, not production code pointing at its own test.

## The sites as of today

```
engine/checks/helpers/active-migrations.mjs:103
engine/pack_loader/pack-schema.mjs:72
engine/scheduler/queue/prework-run.mjs:3
engine/scheduler/run.mjs:10
engine/scheduler/signals/index.mjs:35
engine/scheduler/slots.mjs:18
packs/claudinite-dashboard/model.mjs:11
packs/claudinite-dashboard/tasks/fleet-digest/dated-fixture-collision.mjs:4
packs/claudinite-growth/capture-log.mjs:14, :36
packs/claudinite-lifecycle/rules-index-current.mjs:26, :51
```

Most say the same thing — "a guard pins this" — and lose nothing by naming the guard rather than its file, which is how the four in #1066 were resolved.

## Why it is not folded into #1066

Cleaning these touches three more pack directories, so it re-delivers `claudinite-dashboard`, `claudinite-growth` and `claudinite-lifecycle` on their version bumps. That restructure's whole constraint was that members see nothing, so the sweep is its own change.

## Where the check lives

`.claudinite/local/packs/canon-curation/` if it is a canon-corpus rule, or a shared pack if it should reach members — worth deciding first, since the second choice makes it every member's rule and a much wider first run.

input.prompt:
You are triaging GitHub issues in repo missingbulb/Claudinite as part of the `tidy-issues` maintenance task. Use ONLY the mcp__github__* MCP tools for GitHub access (issue_read, issue_write, add_issue_comment, get_label, list_issue_fields). You also have local repo access at /home/user/Claudinite (already `git fetch origin main`-ed; origin/main tip is e26e0c188fbd7b11c702babc89d4014bda1f4716) via Bash/Grep/Read — use `git show origin/main:<path>` or `git grep <pattern> origin/main -- <path>` to check what's actually true of main's CURRENT content. Do not check out or modify any branch; read-only against origin/main.

Triage EACH of these issue numbers, one at a time, independently: 334, 590, 840, 996, 1003, 991, 766, 952, 223, 920

## The triage ladder — take the FIRST applicable action per issue

1. **Already implemented in `main`** → verify the issue's actual ask is true of origin/main's content NOW (never infer from a linked PR merging or the issue "looking" done) → **close** it (issue_write: state=closed, state_reason=completed) + post a one-line comment citing exactly where/how it's true in main (file/behavior), ending with the marker below.
2. **Conflicts with a current guideline/rule in the repo** (e.g. contradicts something in CLAUDE.md / packs/*/RULES.md as currently written) → apply label `needs-decision` (get current labels first — see label-safety note below) + comment naming the conflict, ending with the marker.
3. **Blocked by another issue** (that other issue is open and must land first) → apply label `blocked` + comment `blocked by #N`, ending with the marker.
4. **Small and quick to do** (a well-scoped, low-risk change) → apply label `quick-win` + comment scoping what the quick fix is, ending with the marker.
5. **Else** → leave it untouched. Take no action, post nothing.

### Checkbox signal
If EVERY checkbox in the issue body is ticked, that's the author's own claim of completion — a reason to run the "implemented in main" check (rung 1), never proof by itself. Verified true in main ⇒ close citing where. Not verified ⇒ comment naming what's still missing (this IS an action — it's a comment, so log it, but do NOT close). A partially-ticked list is not a completion signal at all — triage as if no boxes existed. If the ask has NO repo-side artifact (e.g., a console/platform setting only a human can touch), the author's own ticks are the closing condition — say so in your comment and close.

### Never re-post a verdict already posted
Before doing anything, read the issue's existing comments (issue_read method=get_comments). Find the most recent comment ending in a `<!-- claudinite:tidy-issues verdict=... -->` marker (or, for an issue triaged before the marker existed, one that clearly restates this same verdict in wording). If the action you're about to take is the SAME action that comment already announced, take NO action and NO comment — record this issue's outcome as `unchanged` (note: "<action> since <date>"). Closing is never a repeat — it changes the issue's actual state, so if the issue is still open and your verdict is "close", always execute the close even if a prior comment argued for it.

### Marker
End every comment you post (whether it's a close comment, needs-decision, blocked, quick-win, or a "still missing" comment) with this exact line alone at the end:
```
<!-- claudinite:tidy-issues verdict=<action> -->
```
where `<action>` is one of: closed, needs-decision, blocked, quick-win (use `closed` even for the "still missing, not closing" case is WRONG — for that case, since you did NOT close, there is no verdict action from the ladder; skip posting a marker-bearing comment for that sub-case only if you're unsure, but generally: if you post a comment about missing work under the checkbox path without closing, treat it as a regular open triage note and do not apply a verdict marker since it isn't a ladder outcome — just leave it uncommented in that edge case and record it as `left`).

### Label safety
GitHub's issue-update label field REPLACES the full label set, it doesn't add to it. Before applying `needs-decision`/`blocked`/`quick-win`, call issue_read method=get_labels to get the issue's CURRENT labels, then call issue_write method=update with labels = (existing labels ∪ {new label}), deduplicated. If get_label shows the label doesn't exist in the repo yet, still include it in the issue_write labels array (GitHub auto-creates on issue update in most configs); if the write errors, note the failure in your report but still post the comment (the comment is the actual triage signal).

## What NOT to do
- Never touch PRs, branches, or push code. Never comment on or close a PR even if a number here happens to be one (check first: issue_read get gets you `pull_request`-shaped data if it's actually a PR — if so, skip it and note "is a PR, not an issue, skipped").
- Never invent implementation status — cite exact file paths / content from origin/main.
- Don't over-post: if uncertain, prefer "left" over guessing.

## Output format
When done with all 10 issues, report back a plain list, one line per issue, EXACTLY in this format:
`#<number>: <action> — <one-sentence note>`
where `<action>` is one of: closed, needs-decision, blocked, quick-win, left, unchanged, skipped-pr.
This is your entire deliverable — return just this list (10 lines), nothing else.
