[{"id":5316661692,"body":"Two more findings from the same adoption, on the owner's instruction to keep them here rather than open separate issues. Both are about **how a human-handover step is written**, so they sit one level up from the path bug above — that one is a wrong address, these are a wrong shape.

## 1. A GitHub settings step must be a deep link, not a breadcrumb trail

The handover issue this adoption produced said things like:

> Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions → New repository secret

Every one of those is a URL the agent already knows how to construct — it has the `owner/repo` — so making the human navigate is pure friction, and a breadcrumb goes stale the moment GitHub reorganizes a settings page while a URL keeps redirecting. The rule the owner asked for: **hyperlink every requested GitHub setting change, to the deepest page that exists.**

The patterns worth naming wherever this lands:

| Step | URL |
|---|---|
| New Actions secret | `https://github.com///settings/secrets/actions/new` |
| Actions secrets and variables | `https://github.com///settings/secrets/actions` |
| Workflow permissions, Actions general | `https://github.com///settings/actions` |
| Auto-merge, merge methods, general | `https://github.com///settings` |
| Branch protection / rulesets | `https://github.com///settings/branches` |
| Environments | `https://github.com///settings/environments` |

This is general to every repo the fleet adopts, not specific to the one that hit it — which is why it is here and not in that repo's local pack.

## 2. Don't ask a human to enable something GitHub enables by default

The same issue carried a checkbox for **Settings → General → "Allow squash merging"**, on the reasoning that the merge recipe squashes always. But GitHub enables all three merge methods on a new repository, so the box could only ever be already-ticked. A handover list whose items are mostly no-ops teaches the reader to skim it, which is exactly the failure mode a handover list exists to prevent.

Worth stating as a rule where the handover shape is defined: **a handover step must name a change from the platform's default.** If the default already satisfies the requirement, the requirement is met and there is nothing to hand over.

Both corrections are applied in the consuming repo's own issue ([missingbulb/Shepherd#3](https://github.com/missingbulb/Shepherd/issues/3)) — this is the upstream half, so the next adoption does not repeat either.

One consequence of keeping all three here: this issue's title now names only the first finding. Worth retitling to something like *"bootstrap.md Part 9 path bug, plus two rules for writing human-handover steps"* if it is going to be triaged by title.

{"number":1235,"title":"Chain 1/3: force the twice-daily cron onto every member, and read it back","body":"Link 1 of #1225's execution chain. You will never see the conversation that planned this — everything you need is here.

```
Blocked-by: #1231
Model: sonnet
```

## What changed, and why this needs forcing

The scheduler cron went from hourly to twice daily (`docs/tasks-dispatch/DESIGN.md` §17): ` ,<(dailyHour+12)%24> * * *`. That is a change to a contract members' own files must satisfy — a workflow file plus a frequency vocabulary — so the nightly converge is not enough on its own to answer *"did it work on every repo?"*.

## What makes this step's world ready

#1231 closed, meaning #1230 merged. The queue holds this until then.

## The playbook

1. Drive Shepherd's `fleet-baseline` with `follow`, so it converges every member and reports per member rather than dispatching and returning.
2. For **each** member, read two things from the member's own repo:
   - its stamp's `packVersions` — `claudinite-lifecycle` ≥ `60822.2`, `claudinite-growth` ≥ `60822.1`, `claudinite-dashboard` ≥ `60822.2`;
   - its `.github/workflows/claudinite-scheduler.yml` `cron:` line.
3. The cron is member-specific. Compute the expected value rather than matching a constant: `node engine/scheduler/hash-minute.mjs ` for the minute, and the member's own `taskScheduler.dailyHour` (default 4) for the hours — so a default member expects ` 4,16 * * *`.

## What counts as this step having worked

Every member reads back **both** the stamped pack versions and its own correct two-tick cron.

The workflow file is the half that can lag: `.github/workflows/` is the one path a converge cannot push, so it lands through the member's `update` task apply-stage PR. A member whose stamp has moved but whose workflow PR is still open has **not** passed — note it and keep this issue open; it will pass on a later run once that PR lands.

## When the check fails

Comment what you actually read, per member, and **leave this issue open**. Closing is what releases the next link, so a failed step must not close.

A member you cannot read is a failure, not a pass. A scope-blocked or rate-limited sweep answers "all clear" in exactly the way a healthy fleet does — if a read did not succeed, say so rather than counting it.

## How it ends

Comment the per-member evidence on #1225, then close this issue as completed. That close releases Link 2.

{"number":1187,"title":"Resolve a canon pack's id against its whole tree, unfreezing seven stalled members","body":"Closes #1186

Seven members have not landed a mount update since ~10 August. Each runs its converge daily, opens a PR, and the PR is parked:

> **needs-human** — the converged tree FAILED its self-test — the machinery that runs the rules is not intact

## The bug

`RENAMED_PACKS` holds two shapes that read identically in the map:

| shape | what the tree holds |
|---|---|
| **rename** (`core` → `claudinite-lifecycle`) | one directory — the migration record's `aliases` moves it |
| **absorption** (`github-actions` → `git-github`, #1057/#1079) | **both** directories — there is no record, and the pack flow "never removes a tree that has stopped being declared" (its own words, `2026-08-19-pack-renames/migration.mjs`) |

`scanPackDir` canonicalized a canon pack's own id from the map alone. Correct for a rename; for an absorption it put two live directories on one id, so the collision guard dropped **both**:

```
pack id "chrome-extension" is declared twice — by the canon and the canon
pack id "git-github" is declared twice — by the canon and the canon
```

That fails the `pack-manifests` probe → the converged tree fails its self-test → the converge parks its own PR. The leftover directory is only ever removed by a converge that lands, so the member re-derives the same broken tree every day. A closed loop.

It surfaced on 10 August because members' current `main` runs the older engine, which does not canonicalize a canon pack's own id — so `main` self-tests clean while the branch fails, which is why the members look healthy: green runs, green `main`, nothing merging.

## The change

The map can't distinguish the two shapes, but the tree can. The id is now resolved once the whole canon scan is known: an absorbed leftover whose survivor is present keeps its own id and goes inert — what an id nothing declares is meant to do. A member still declaring the absorbed spelling is unaffected, since the declaration side resolves onto the survivor, which is live.

## Verification

Against `missingbulb/CrosswordChat`#249's **actual head**, with only this change vendored in:

```
before   Claudinite self-test: 1 of 6 probes FAILED — pack-manifests
         2 pack(s) failed to load or validate
after    Claudinite self-test: 6 probes passed.          (discoverPacks: 0 errors)
```

- New `engine-tests/pack_loader/renamed-packs.test.mjs` — 4 tests covering both shapes and the no-duplicates property; written first and watched fail on the missing export.
- Full suite: 2503 pass, 1 fail — `engine-pack-lane-shims`, which is the shallow-clone guard firing on this session's own checkout (`git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository` → `true`). It walks pack history and touches nothing in this diff.
- `check_the_work` and `check_the_world`: 0 blocking.

**This reaches the frozen members with no per-repo hand-running** — the self-test runs against the converged tree, so the next converge vendors the fixed loader and the probe passes.

## Folders touched

**`engine/pack_loader/`** — `renamed-packs.mjs` gains `canonicalPackIdAmong`, which only maps an id forward when the target isn't already present in the tree; `pack-registry.mjs` carries each canon pack's raw id through `scanPackDir` and re-resolves the whole set in `discoverPacks`, where the full tree is known.

## Not in this change

The absorbed leftovers stay on disk as inert, undeclared trees — harmless now, but dead weight that nothing prunes. Worth its own issue (the fix is a migration record that *deletes* rather than moves, since the survivor's directory already exists); deliberately kept out of the change that unfreezes the fleet.

{"number":1236,"title":"Chain 2/3: verify the twice-daily cron in production — 2 scheduler runs a day, not 24","body":"Link 2 of #1225's execution chain. Everything you need is here.

```
Blocked-by: #1235
Not-before: 2026-08-25T06:00:00Z
Retry-every: 1 day
Model: sonnet
```

## What this proves

The whole point of the change: the scheduler was **71% of private Actions spend** at ~26 min/day per member, because Actions bills each job rounded up and the cron fired 24 times a day to do about 13 minutes of work. Two ticks a day should make that ~2 min/day. Nothing so far has measured a real repo — only the simulator.

## What makes this step's world ready

#1235 closed (every member on the new cron), **and** at least one full UTC day has elapsed since, so there is a complete day to count.

## What to observe

For each **private** member — the ones that cost anything; public repos are free and unlimited:

1. **The count.** Scheduler workflow runs for one complete UTC day. Expect exactly **2**. Baseline: 24.
2. **Nothing was dropped.** No task's standing item is missing its occurrence for that day — a cheaper cron that quietly stopped instantiating work is a regression, not a saving.
3. **The risk the simulator could not model.** A whole day's chain now settles serially inside one executor run. Read the longest executor run's duration against the workflow's `timeout-minutes: 350`. The simulator's task durations are fixtures, so this is the first real read of whether a member's day actually fits.

## What counts as this step having worked

Every private member shows 2 scheduler runs for the measured day, no missing occurrences, and no executor run near its timeout.

## When the check fails

Comment what you read and **leave this issue open** — closing releases the next link.

- Still 24 runs on some member → its workflow never landed; reopen #1235's question there rather than proceeding.
- Missing occurrences → this is a real regression in the cadence change. Reopen #1225 with what is missing and stop the chain.
- An executor run near the timeout → do **not** fail the step, but say so plainly on #1225: it is the residual risk the plan named, and it wants its own issue rather than silence.

## How it ends

Comment the per-member figures on #1225 — runs/day before and after, and the longest executor run — then close this issue as completed. That close releases Link 3.

{"number":1105,"title":"Engine and pack versions become date-anchored `<day>.<n>`","body":"Closes #1100.

Versions were a plain monotonic counter. It orders releases, which is all the update flows need, but it says nothing about *when* one was cut: a member stamped at `6` against a canon at `13` is behind by an unknown amount of time, and every fleet surface reporting that gap makes a reader go and date it by hand.

Both the engine and every pack now version as `.` — `60820.1`, where the day part is `(year - 2020) * 10000 + month * 100 + day` and the second part is the running number of versions cut that day. Displayed with a leading `v`, as the surfaces already do.

Two decisions worth naming:

- **The year is anchored on 2020, not taken as its last digit.** A last-digit year wraps to `0` in 2030 and sorts a decade of releases underneath every 2029 one. `2026 → 6` either way, so the example holds and the ordering survives.
- **A version is a string.** `60820.10` and `60820.1` are different versions and the same float, so nothing in the corpus may parse one as a number.

### The migration technique

Every reader accepts **both** spellings. A legacy integer parses as `.0`, which sorts below every date-anchored version — exactly where a member that has not re-stamped belongs, so no fleet surface has to special-case it. The tolerance is scheduled for removal in its own change, #1106, once the fleet has converged; the parser's own comment carries that date and issue number.

Legacy integers deliberately stay in two places for now: each pack's `minEngineVersion` floor and every migration record's `version:` range, both of which are references to engine versions that really were plain counters. #1106 retires them.

Zero stays readable and is *not* a legacy version — it is the install floor (DESIGN §3), so `isVersion(0)` is true while `isDeclaredVersion(0)` is false, and a stamp at the floor still reads as "says something" rather than as absence.

### What changed, by folder

- **`engine/`** — `version.mjs` gains the format: `parseVersion`, `compareVersions`, `versionsEqual`, `nextVersion`, `versionDay`, and `VERSION_SOURCE`, the regex fragment the text scrapers share so the six of them cannot disagree about what a version looks like. The helpers live beside the constant rather than in a module of their own, so the engine surface a mount must carry for any of it is one file. `ENGINE_VERSION` becomes `'60820.1'`. `pack_loader/pack-schema.mjs` validates both spellings, and `checks/helpers/active-migrations.mjs` reads a record's range and ranges over it through the shared comparator.
- **`updates/`** — the three planners (`engine-update`, `pack-update`, `install`) compare through `versionAbove` instead of `>` and gate on `isVersion` instead of `typeof === 'number'`.
- **`packs/`** — all 33 manifests move to `'60820.1'`. The dashboard's `fleet.mjs` and the sheepdog's `fleet-roster/drift-issues.mjs` scrape and compare through the shared helpers.
- **`.claudinite/local/packs/`** — `pack-version-bumped` and `engine-release-record`, the two canon-side checks that read a version out of a diff, do the same; the first now names `nextVersion(base)` as the remedy rather than `base + 1`.
- **`vendoring/rehearsal/fixtures.mjs`** — the `versioned-local` shape gains a second local pack carrying the date-anchored spelling. This is the `consumer-safe-change` answer: the manifest vocabulary widened, additively, and the fixture is what proves a consumer-authored manifest still validates in **both** spellings.

`ENGINE_VERSION` moving is an engine release, so it lands with its `RELEASES.md` row citing canary rehearsal [run 32371130795](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/actions/runs/32371130795), dispatched against this branch at `1f05d43`.

### One unrelated commit, and why it is here

The second commit fixes `a long work step leaves heartbeats on its own item`, which slept a fixed 40ms against a 5ms beat interval and asserted two beats had arrived. It is red on `origin/main` — three full-suite runs out of four at eight workers — and it was red on this branch's CI twice in a row, so nothing was going to make this PR green without it. The step now polls its own item until the second beat lands, under a 5s ceiling so a heartbeat that never fires stays a failed assertion rather than a hang. It is a separate commit and nothing else in the diff touches the scheduler.

### On delivery

This changes a contract member files carry (the stamp) and the engine flow that reads it, so "will it work on every repo?" is a live question rather than a uniform-by-construction change. Driving Shepherd's `fleet-baseline` with `follow`, and reporting per member, belongs to whoever merges this.

Status note from the #649 verification run; the blocker here is unchanged.

**Still blocked by #239** — the `FLEET_GITHUB_TOKEN` Contents-write grant on the home repo. Nothing today touches that, and the four `.github/workflows/chrome-extension-*.yml` files plus the two actions are still in `main`'s `.github/`.

Two things about this issue's *phase 1* did change, though.

**The delivery mechanism this plan rests on has now been proven live.** The plan's step 2 is "a **materialize** op — [the update flow] writes the vendored set into each consumer's `.github/`", and `chrome-release-vendoring` has carried exactly that since #280. But a record materializing into `.github/workflows/` had **never actually run against a live member** — that is the residual #649 was reopened for and the last open item on #768. Until today, phase 1 was landed code whose delivery step was untested; if it had been broken, the first consumer to converge would have failed its whole update, not just that file (the Action token's refusal rejects the entire ref).

Verified end to end on the canary on 2026-08-14 (evidence on #649): the record's write is withheld to `.claudinite/pending-workflows/`, rides the PR as a reviewable added file, the update parks at `apply-stage`, and a session moves it into `.github/workflows/` byte-for-byte. So `chrome-release-vendoring` should now be expected to deliver when its consumers converge.

**The vocabulary here is stale.** This issue says "baselining (not the consumer) owns keeping the copies correct" and "baselining materializes it". {"number":840,"title":"Engine-driven format changes to consumer-held files need a first-class migration class","body":"Owner decision context (2026-08-14, on #564): converting members' local `pack.mjs` files to `pack.json` rides a `basics` pack record with `applyStage` — but the owner flagged the routing itself as the gap: *"this is a classic 'engine changed, the format of local packs should change' migration."*

The gap: the **engine** owns the local-pack manifest format, but the engine flow may carry no agentic work (versioned-updates DESIGN §5), and its declarative ops (`aliases`/`materialize`/`rewrite`/`declarePacks`) cannot express "reshape this member-authored file". So every engine-side format change to a consumer-held file gets routed ad-hoc through whichever pack is convenient (`basics`, because it is declared everywhere) — the same shape as the #555 manifest tightening, which shipped with *no* carrier and broke eleven local packs silently.

Ask: make "the engine changed a format consumers hold" a recognized migration class with a designated carrier — so the record can be authored where the change lives (with the engine), while the member-side session it needs runs through the one agentic lane that exists (the pack flow), without each occurrence re-deriving the routing. `legacyPresent` telemetry and the retirement gate should come with the class, not be re-invented per change.

Closing condition: the next engine-owned format change to a consumer-held file has an obvious, documented place to land, and the pack.json conversion's routing (via `basics`) is either retroactively blessed as that place or superseded by it.","state":"open","html_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/840","user":{"login":"missingbulb","id":73882448,"profile_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/73882448?v=4"},"author_association":"OWNER","labels":["quick-win"],"assignees":[],"comments":2,"reactions":{"total_count":0,"+1":0,"-1":0,"laugh":0,"confused":0,"heart":0,"hooray":0,"rocket":0,"eyes":0},"created_at":"2026-08-14T18:43:43Z","updated_at":"2026-08-19T05:18:51Z","has_parent":false,"has_children":false,"closed_by_pull_requests":{"total_count":0,"references":[]}}

{"number":1165,"title":"claudinite-dashboard: a usage-backed data plane, the repo page rebuilt, and repo/fleet modes","body":"Implements the code half of #1158 — PRs 1–4 of its stack, as one review pass.

## The idea

The page reads **two kinds of data and treats them differently**. What is true right now is a handful of live, ETag-revalidated reads. What happened before is one file per repo — `.claudinite/local/usage.GENERATED.json`, keyed by the head sha, so it is read once when `main` moves and not at all while it has not.

Measured against a stubbed API (one repo, five declared tasks):

| | Requests | Free |
|---|---|---|
| Cold | 14 | 0 |
| Warm (same head sha) | 5 | **5** — every one a `304` |

A warm reload of a repo page costs nothing against the viewer's budget.

## The data plane (`usage-fold`)

Hourly now, gated on the repo having moved this hour — a commit on the default branch or a session that captured. A quiet hour declines and loses nothing: the REST reads are watermarked, and the dashboard tops up its freshest hours from the run listing it already fetches.

New in the file: an **hour tier** (72h of scheduler runs, executor runs, agent sessions and what they executed); the **queue's own closed items** per task per outcome — the queue-era successor to the retired slot-scheduler census, closing #994; **rule tokens per session** off the mount's own session-start line; **token spend** probed from the transcripts' usage records; **commits and lines** from local git; **releases**; and a `generated` stamp excluded from the unchanged-compare so a quiet repo still opens no PR.

The slot scheduler's per-task log reader is retired with it: nothing has written those records since #974, so it spent two API calls per run finding none.

Throughout, an absent source leaves **no key** rather than a zero — a day before a shallow checkout's history begins, a transcript shape carrying no usage — and a week only sums the days that knew.

## The repo page

At-a-glance tiles (minutes waiting on a person and what they are made of, parks, PRs and issues, CI, runs in flight, stars, drift against the canon). **One work table** in place of the roster and queue tables, which were the same rows twice: three views — stuck / pending / all — over one row model, each with the columns its own question needs, opening on the worst non-empty one, rows moving rather than being redrawn when you switch. Per-day queue outcomes, a 48-hour runs graph with the tasks that executed in each hour on hover, and 30 days of rule tokens against checks executed on two stated scales.

## The fleet page

The roster is **enumerated as the viewer** from a configured `owner`, not stored: a repo someone cannot read is not in their fleet. The sweep reads each member's usage file at the sha it already has, which gives the fleet page the two figures its own note used to name as absent — check findings caught, and what the corpus costs each session. A member that folds nothing is named, never averaged in.

That is the last thing `usage-fleet.GENERATED.json` was needed for; retiring it is filed separately, blocked behind this.

## Modes

Which dashboard a deployment builds is decided by its config's **shape** — a roster source means fleet, anything else means that repo — so there is nothing to ask at adoption and no way to configure a roster and still get the wrong landing page.

## Folders this change touched

```
packs/claudinite-growth/tasks/usage-fold/
    the fold: an hour tier, the queue's closed items, rule tokens, token spend,
    git and release series, a freshness stamp; hourly on a movement precondition.
    read-task-runs.mjs retired, read-runs.mjs and read-queue.mjs in its place.

packs/claudinite-dashboard/
    usage.mjs      — reads a member's usage file, decoding against the file's OWN
                     declared vocabulary so this pack imports nothing from that one
    work.mjs       — the one work-row model behind the three views
    fleet-growth.mjs — the fleet's corpus series, and the coverage census, derived live
    canon.mjs      — the canon-version read, shared by both views
    view-repo.mjs  — rewritten around the above
    view-fleet.mjs — reads member usage; canon read moved out
    config.mjs     — owner enumeration, and the mode test
    github.mjs     — listOwnerRepos; cache.mjs projects a run's workflow path
    ui.mjs         — dual-axis chart, FLIP row transitions, and a column-gap fix the
                     48-hour panel found (fixed 3 units went negative past ~33 columns)
    build-site.mjs — repo vs fleet mode, reported in the build summary

engine/scheduler/signals/
    conversationLogs carries the NEWEST log's age beside the oldest — the only
    newness that dimension had, and what the fold's precondition gates on
```

## Verification

- Full suite green (2462 tests); `check_the_work` clean; `check_the_world` clean of anything in the files this touches.
- Both pages driven in a real browser against a stubbed API — no console or page errors, the view switcher exercised, cold/warm request counts as above. That run is what found the chart's negative column widths.
- Both modes built from real declarations: `mode: repo-dashboard` for this repo, `mode: fleet-dashboard` for a declaration naming an owner.

--- 2026-07-26T19:14:27Z https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/394#issuecomment-5084985912
## Phase 3 pre-flight: the competing-cron census

The Phase 3 blocker is per-repo crons — `gha/no-scheduled-fleet-executor` is blocking and, once `claudinite-scheduler.yml` lands, flags *every other* `schedule:`, so a repo cut over without converting its product crons goes red in the same commit. This is that census, done ahead of the clones.

**It corrects the survey in #424.**

| Repo | Crons to convert | Verified |
|---|---|---|
| **TLDR** | **1** — `chrome-extension-release.yml`, `cron: "0 3 * * *"` | partial |
| **CrosswordChat** | **1** — `chrome-extension-release.yml`, `cron: "30 0 * * *"` | partial |
| **EdFringeNow** | **17 lines / 2 workflows** — `refresh.yml` (`20 5 * * *`) and `refresh-tickets.yml` (16 August-only hourly lines, `9 7 * 8 *` … `8 22 * 8 *`) | ✅ full |
| LaughCounter | none — `build-macos-dmg` (push/dispatch), `release-macos-dmg` (push/release/dispatch) | ✅ full |
| HelloWorldFlutterApp | none — `build` (push/dispatch), `debug` (dispatch) | ✅ full |
| EdFringeAllocator | none — `fetch.yml` is `workflow_dispatch` only | ✅ full |
| Sheepdog | none — no `.github/workflows/` | ✅ full |
| ShoutsAndWhispers | none — no `.github/workflows/` | ✅ full |
| gRatio | none — no `.github/workflows/` (per #424, not re-verified) | unverified |

### The correction

#424's table said **TLDR: none — `chrome-extension-*` are called reusables, no scheduled orchestrator.** That is wrong. The *reusables* carry no cron, but the **orchestrator** `chrome-extension-release.yml` does: `schedule: cron "0 3 * * *"`. Cutting TLDR over without converting it would have gone red on the cutover commit — exactly the failure mode that row was written to prevent. CrosswordChat has the same shape at `30 0 * * *`.

Both are the `store-release` case: the task's precondition detects a deployable change and the worker dispatches the release workflow, which drops its own cron. Same conversion GCEC already had — its `chrome-extension-release.yml` now carries a "No cron here: the Claudinite scheduler's store-release task … dispatches this workflow" header, which is the shape to copy.

### Method, and why two rows say "partial"

Every "full" row was verified by reading each workflow's `on:` block directly (or `grep -rn "cron:"` over a clone, for EdFringeNow).

**GitHub code search was unreliable and I discarded it.** `cron user:missingbulb path:.github/workflows` returned 5 hits and reported **zero** for EdFringeNow — which actually has 17 cron lines. A search hit is trustworthy; a search *miss* is not evidence of absence. That's what the TLDR and CrosswordChat rows rest on for their *other* workflows (8 and 4 respectively, unread), so those two are marked partial: the cron listed is confirmed present, but I can't yet promise it's the only one. One `grep -rn "cron:" .github/workflows/` per repo closes it at clone time.

### Why this is a comment and not a branch

This session's environment is fd-exhausted — `environment-manager` holds 4095 of 4096 descriptors, so the git proxy 502s on every clone and the commit signer times out. The census was gathered entirely over the GitHub API, which still works. Phase 3's actual work (vendor refresh, scheduler workflow, `taskScheduler` key) needs checkouts and can't start until that clears.

Refs #394.
